transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-18 15:30 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Ashley Kim (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Cascade Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (Cascade CTO), Sofia Mendes (Cascade SecOps)

Auto summary (auto-generated): Security-focused discovery to validate Redwood private/dedicated options for regulated data, discuss KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and perform eval parity checks vs current OpenAI-based deployment.

Topics: Security reqs, deployment modes, model compatibility, benchmarks, pilot criteria.

-- Transcript body --
[00:00:00] Ashley: Hi everyone, thanks for blocking time. I'm Ashley from Redwood, AE on this account, with Marco, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:08] Priya: Hey Ashley, hi Marco. Doing well, thanks. Sofia and Liam are on as well. We — Cascade's security team is leading this effort so you'll probably hear a lot of questions about keys and logs.
[00:00:17] Liam: Yep, hi. We're looking at alternatives to OpenAI because of recent cost and latency spikes and also because we need tighter control over residency.
[00:00:25] Marco: Great, thanks. Quick agenda from our side: understand current stack, walk requirements, map to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, and talk about compatibility with vLLM/TGI stacks and eval parity.
[00:00:34] Sofia: Sounds good. I'll jump in on compliance — SOC2 is table stakes, but we also need KMS integration, HSM support, and provable audit logs for all inference requests.
[00:00:45] Ashley: Understood. Can you describe your current flow? Where does the data live today and which models are you using with OpenAI?
[00:00:52] Priya: Right now we send PII-filtered payloads to OpenAI via a mid-tier service. We're mainly using gpt-4-like endpoints for summarization and entity extraction, plus embeddings for search. We also have an internal pilot using vLLM on GPU for some on-prem experimentation.
[00:01:05] Marco: Okay. Two quick clarifying q's — one: when you say "on-prem experimentation with vLLM," is that full production or just a lab? Two: is the goal to run everything on- premises eventually?
[00:01:14] Priya: It's lab for now. We want a hybrid outcome: some sensitive workloads on private (VPC/on-prem) and others in a Dedicated Redwood pool.
[00:01:22] Sofia: And we need to ensure the private runtime integrates with our KMS — we use AWS KMS and have an HSM-backed key for envelope keys.
[00:01:30] Marco: We do that — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and can point to your HSM-backed keys for model artifacts and audit signing. We can also fingerprint and sign inference responses if you need.
[00:01:41] Liam: Fingerprint? Could you expand? We need tamper-evidence in logs and chain-of-custody for requests.
[00:01:47] Marco: Sure, sorry, quick jargon — by fingerprinting I mean we can generate a signed hash of the request/response pair stored in immutable audit logs. That can be validated later against your signing key in HSM.
[00:02:00] Sofia: That sounds promising. How about SSO and RBAC? We have SAML 2.0, SCIM provisioning, and need role separation between devs and SecOps.
[00:02:08] Ashley: Redwood supports SSO with SAML and SCIM provisioning for user syncs. RBAC is configurable per route and model. We can also give token-level audit views to SecOps.
[00:02:17] Priya: Good. On the model side, compatibility is key. Our devs have tuned prompts against OpenAI APIs and some local TGI experiments. We need parity checks — quality and latency. How do you handle that?
[00:02:27] Marco: Two parts: model compatibility and operational parity. For compatibility, Redwood hosts curated open models and can deploy customer-provided model files. For eval parity, we recommend a two-week benchmark using your prompt set against the target model variants and our Dedicated runtime. We'll measure latency P50/P95 and token cost, and run qualitative evals against your rubric.
[00:02:42] Liam: Can you run the eval against both a hosted Redwood-managed model and a Private deployment? We want to see differences in latency and any diff in outputs.
[00:02:50] Marco: Yes, we can run against Hosted and a Dedicated pool in your VPC, assuming network paths are set. For Private air-gapped, we'd need a short on- prem deployment; that's doable but has a longer timeline.
[00:02:59] Sofia: Network-wise we can't expose production traffic to any third-party endpoints. Would Dedicated with VPC peering be acceptable?
[00:03:07] Ashley: Many customers do Dedicated with customer VPC peering — you retain network control and traffic does not traverse public internet. We can also do a Private deployment with your control plane.
[00:03:16] Priya: Pricing and commits — how does Dedicated compare to Hosted? We need to justify the fixed cost.
[00:03:22] Ashley: Dedicated is reserved capacity — more predictable unit costs, and you get isolation. Hosted is pay-as-you-go but can be more expensive at high volume. We can run a cost model using your token volumes.
[00:03:31] Liam: Do you support quantized model variants? We have a workflow that benefits from 4-bit quantized models to save cost.
[00:03:37] Marco: Yes, the runtime supports quantization-friendly paths and we can suggest profiles. We'll capture quality delta during the eval. vLLM and TGI experiments — if you have LM artifacts from those workflows, we can load them and run parity tests.
[00:03:49] Priya: One red flag we've seen is slight differences in extraction outputs when moving away from OpenAI. Even a small F1 drop is a problem. How do you surface regression?
[00:03:58] Marco: We set up automated evals tied to your prompt set and metrics. If we detect regressions, we can recommend alternative model variants or fallback to a higher-capacity model. Also we keep model version pinning so you can rollback.
[00:04:09] Sofia: Audit logs — how granular are they? We need request/response metadata, auth id, model version, and the hash you mentioned.
[00:04:16] Marco: We emit request-level logs with metadata, which can be shipped to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3. The signed-hash is optional but recommended for tamper evidence.
[00:04:25] Priya: About data retention — we need to ensure we can set retention to 30 days for raw logs and longer for aggregated metrics.
[00:04:31] Ashley: Retention is configurable for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has default retention but we can negotiate enterprise retention for contracts.
[00:04:40] Liam: Ok, let's talk technical deep dive — can Marco outline the baseline steps for the SE benchmark?
[00:04:45] Marco: Sure. We'll need: 1) your canonical prompt set and sample payloads; 2) a small dataset of labeled outputs for quality eval; 3) your expected qps and latency targets; 4) access to a test VPC for Dedicated runs or sample artifacts for Private. We'll run the prompts across model variants (open-ggml/openllama/mistral-like etc) and also against your vLLM run if you can provide container images or model files. Results go into a shared spreadsheet with token counts, P50/P95 latencies, and qualitative scores.
[00:05:20] Priya: We can provide prompts and labeled rubric. For vLLM, it's currently experimental but we can package the model files.
[00:05:26] Ashley: Great. Timing — Marco suggested a benchmark window of 3-5 business days to iterate, with final review the following week. Does that align?
[00:05:33] Liam: Yes, that timeline works for us.
[00:05:36] Sofia: A few corner questions: 1) Can you support FIPS-certified crypto in the Private deployment? 2) Do your audit logs include payload redaction policy?
[00:05:45] Marco: For FIPS, Private deployments can be configured against an environment that uses FIPS modules; we should validate in the SOW. For payload redaction, we support automatic PII redaction hooks pre-send and you can configure what fields to drop from logs.
[00:05:58] Priya: Great. About incident response — we need a process for suspected data exfiltration from a model. Can you help with playbooks?
[00:06:05] Ashley: Yes, we have incident playbooks for Dedicated and Private customers. We can include escalation contacts and a runbook in the security packet.
[00:06:12] Liam: One more ops question — how do you handle canary rollouts and model versioning? We want to do gradual rollouts and auto-fallback.
[00:06:19] Marco: Redwood supports canary rollouts and traffic split routing by route. We have automatic rollback policies if latency or error rates cross thresholds.
[00:06:26] Priya: Pricing again — can we get a sample cost comparison for our 2m tokens/month profile with a Dedicated baseline vs Hosted?
[00:06:33] Ashley: We'll prepare a model-based cost sheet. I'll need a rough token/month and peak concurrency, but we can also run an example using your sampled traces.
[00:06:41] Sofia: For the benchmark, can you also capture generation determinism? We need to ensure that embeddings and extraction are repeatable between runs for auditability.
[00:06:49] Marco: We'll capture determinism metrics and config the RNG seeds where applicable; we'll surface any nondeterministic behavior in the report.
[00:06:58] Priya: Ok that checks a lot of boxes. Any limitations or caveats we should be aware of?
[00:07:03] Marco: Only that Private air-gapped installs require lead time for install, and some enterprise features like long-term storage of raw token logs may require contract amendments. Also, some smaller open models can show quality gaps vs larger proprietary models, so the eval is important.
[00:07:18] Liam: Understood.
[00:07:20] Ashley: Quick note — Marco mentioned we can do signed hashes and HSM integration. I'll attach our SOC2 and security packet, and Marco will run the baseline.
[00:07:29] Priya: Perfect. One more ask — our legal team will want a data flow diagram for the Dedicated option showing no egress. Can you provide that?
[00:07:36] Ashley: Yes, we'll include a VPC peering diagram and data flow detail in the packet.
[00:07:41] Sofia: Great.
[00:07:43] -- 40 minutes later, deeper discussion on prompt-level failure modes and degens --
[00:47:12] Marco: We're seeing in lab that the TGI-based local run had a subtle tokenization diff leading to entity boundary shifts. That's why the qualitative eval is important; sometimes a tokenizer mismatch causes a small but important F1 delta.
[00:47:28] Priya: That's exactly the thing we hit moving some extraction away from OpenAI.
[00:47:34] Marco: We can apply normalization steps in the preprocessing layer or choose a variant with matching tokenizer behavior. We'll document recommended pre/post-processing.
[00:47:42] Liam: On the benchmark spreadsheet can you include a column for tokenizer family and preproc steps?
[00:47:47] Marco: Yes, will do.
[00:47:50] Ashley: Ok, approaching time — recap and explicit next steps. Marco, what do you need to start the SE benchmark?
[00:47:56] Marco: Prompts and labeled dataset, sample model artifacts if you want vLLM parity, test VPC details for Dedicated runs or SSH access window for Private evaluation, and expected traffic profile.
[00:48:08] Priya: We'll share prompts and the rubric by Friday.
[00:48:12] Ashley: I'll send the security packet and SOC 2 and a short SOW template for a pilot.
[00:48:17] Priya: We'll get back with legal on the SOW timing, but the security info is the immediate priority.
[00:48:23] Sofia: And we'll want Marco's spreadsheet before the run so we can add our metrics to it.
[00:48:29] Marco: I'll create a shared sheet and populate initial tabs with latency/cost/quality templates.
[00:48:34] Ashley: Great. Any final questions?
[00:48:36] Liam: No, that's it for now.
[00:48:38] Priya: Thanks, everyone.
[00:48:40] Ashley: Thanks, we'll follow up with docs and schedule the benchmark.
[00:48:45] -- Call ends --
